stem.en: "Deep Water" is taken from

options.en: Of Men and Mountains, the autobiography of William O. Douglas

explanation.en: Deep Water is an extract from Douglas's autobiography Of Men and Mountains.

stem.en: William O. Douglas is best known as

options.en: a Justice of the United States Supreme Court

explanation.en: Douglas served for many years as a Justice of the US Supreme Court.

stem.en: Where did Douglas first become frightened of water?

options.en: In a river during a fishing trip
On a beach in California, when a wave knocked him down

explanation.en: At the age of three or four, a wave knocked him down on a California beach.

stem.en: Which two experiences together created Douglas's fear of water?

options.en: Falling off a boat and getting lost at sea
Watching a friend drown and a flood in his town
A storm at sea and a canoe accident
Being knocked down by a wave as a child and being thrown into the deep end of a pool

explanation.en: The beach wave made him dislike water, and the YMCA pool incident turned that into terror.

stem.en: Why did Douglas think the YMCA pool was safe?

options.en: It was only two or three feet deep at the shallow end
His father was always with him

explanation.en: The shallow end was only two to three feet deep, so it seemed a safe place to learn.

stem.en: What was Douglas's plan after he was thrown into the deep end?

options.en: To spring up from the bottom when his feet touched it
To swim to the side at once

explanation.en: He planned to push up from the bottom, but he rose slowly and sank again.

stem.en: Who threw Douglas into the deep end of the pool?

explanation.en: A big boy, much older than him, picked him up and tossed him in.

stem.en: What happened just before Douglas lost consciousness in the pool?

options.en: He reached the side of the pool
His panic gave way to a strange calm
He shouted for help and was heard

explanation.en: After repeated struggles, the terror eased into a kind of calm, and then he blacked out.

stem.en: How did the instructor keep Douglas safe in the pool?

options.en: With a life jacket and goggles
With a belt attached to a rope over a pulley
By keeping him only in the shallow end

explanation.en: A belt round Douglas was attached to a rope running over a pulley, and the instructor held the rope.

stem.en: In what order did the instructor teach Douglas?

options.en: Breathing out under water and in above it, then kicking with the legs

explanation.en: He learnt breathing first, then kicking, building the whole stroke piece by piece.

stem.en: Which activities did Douglas's fear spoil for years?

explanation.en: Whenever he went near water the terror returned, spoiling fishing trips, canoeing and swimming.

stem.en: Why did Douglas keep testing himself even after the instructor had finished?

options.en: He was not sure the fear had fully gone
He was preparing for a race
He wanted to become a coach

explanation.en: Traces of fear remained, so he swam alone in pools and lakes until he was sure it had gone.

stem.en: What, according to Douglas, was the real thing to be afraid of?

explanation.en: He concluded that the terror lay in the fear of fear, echoing Roosevelt's famous line.

stem.en: Whose idea about fear does Douglas recall at the end?

explanation.en: He recalls Roosevelt's idea that all we have to fear is fear itself.

stem.en: Which quality helped Douglas most to overcome his fear?

explanation.en: His determination to face the fear, together with patient training, helped him succeed.

stem.en: Which statement best expresses the message of "Deep Water"?

options.en: Fear is useful and should be kept
A fear faced patiently and with will power can be overcome

explanation.en: The story shows that fear can be conquered with determination, guidance and gradual practice.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Douglas hired an instructor to teach him swimming.
Reason (R): His fear of water was spoiling many activities that he enjoyed.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: the fear spoilt fishing, canoeing and swimming, so he decided to learn properly.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Douglas learnt to swim within a single day of training.
Reason (R): The instructor taught him one skill at a time.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: the training took months. R is true: he was taught piece by piece.

stem.en: Which step in Arjun's training is most like the instructor's method in "Deep Water"?

options.en: Giving up debates for five years
Speaking to a slowly growing audience week by week

explanation.en: The coach built up Arjun's skill gradually, just as the instructor built a swimmer piece by piece.

passage.en: Arjun, a Class 12 student, froze every time he had to speak on stage after he forgot his lines at a school assembly in Class 7. For five years he avoided debates and even group presentations. This year he joined a public-speaking club. The coach first had him speak to one friend, then to five, then to the whole club, and each week the group grew a little. In February he gave the vote of thanks at the annual day in front of six hundred people, and his voice did not shake.

stem.en: How long had Arjun avoided speaking on stage before he joined the club?

explanation.en: He forgot his lines in Class 7 and avoided debates for five years until Class 12.

passage.en: Arjun, a Class 12 student, froze every time he had to speak on stage after he forgot his lines at a school assembly in Class 7. For five years he avoided debates and even group presentations. This year he joined a public-speaking club. The coach first had him speak to one friend, then to five, then to the whole club, and each week the group grew a little. In February he gave the vote of thanks at the annual day in front of six hundred people, and his voice did not shake.

stem.en: Arrange in order: (A) training with an instructor (B) wave on a California beach (C) swimming across a lake alone (D) thrown into the YMCA pool

explanation.en: Beach wave as a child, then the pool accident, then training, then the solo lake swims.

stem.en: Which statement about "Deep Water" is NOT correct?

options.en: An instructor used a rope and pulley
Douglas's father threw him into the deep end
Douglas later tested himself in lakes

explanation.en: It was a big older boy, not his father, who threw him in.

stem.en: The tone of "Deep Water" is best described as

explanation.en: Douglas reflects honestly on his terror and inspires readers with how he overcame it.
